subject: Staged activation and billing amendment for 8→16 GPU renewal
messages:
From: Mark Gibson <mgibson@evora-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Morris <elaine.m@evora-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions — moving from 8 to 16 GPUs

Hi Olga,

We’re approaching our Nov renewal and the product team has asked whether we can double our dedicated pool from 8→16 GPUs starting on the anniversary. Two quick things we need clarity on before we lock the PO:

1) Can you split activation so we only start billing for the extra 8 GPUs after they’re turned on? We’d like a staged activation over two months.
2) What throughput SLA guarantees will apply once we ramp to 16 (p95 latency targets, sustained tokens/sec)?

Also, finance wants to understand the updated monthly commit and whether there’s any pro-rated billing if activation slips. I attached a draft renewal PO for reference.

Thanks — appreciate a short call if that helps.

—Mark
Head of Platform Engineering
Evora Analytics

Attachment: evora_po_draft.pdf (PDF, 72KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Mark Gibson <mgibson@evora-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Elaine Morris <elaine.m@evora-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — moving from 8 to 16 GPUs

Mark — thanks for the note and the PO. Quick summary up front: we can support a two-stage activation and update the monthly committed units; we just need to align on activation dates, billing start points, and an acceptance test for throughput.

Proposal (high level):
- Contract amendment to change committed pool from 8→16 GPUs, effective on the renewal date (2027-11-01).
- Staged activation: Phase 1 (first 8 GPUs) billing continues as-is; Phase 2 (additional 8 GPUs) will be scheduled to "go live" within 45 days of renewal, billing for the extra capacity starts on the Phase 2 go-live date.
- Throughput guardrails: we’ll provide p95 latency targets and a sustained tokens/sec guidance for your typical sequence distribution; we’ll include a 14-day acceptance window post-phase-2 to validate performance.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Karthik and I will put together a short technical appendix with expected throughput numbers and warm-up guidance.
2) Ben will confirm updated pricing tiers and any transitional credit we can offer for the first 30 days of Phase 2.
3) If Evora agrees, we’ll prepare an amendment and a mutual action plan and route to DocuSign.

If that works, can you confirm preferred Phase 2 latest go-live date (target within 45 days post-renewal or a specific date)?

Cheers,
Olga
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Signature:
Olga Petrov | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0198

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 15:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — moving from 8 to 16 GPUs

Olga / team — digging into the tech plan. TL;DR: staged activation is straightforward; a few constraints and recommendations below.

Operational notes for the appendix:
- Phase 2 warm-up: expect a 48–72 hour warm-up window for KV cache and JIT/compilation stabilization under steady traffic. During that window, tail latency can be ~1.2–1.5x baseline for short sequences.
- Throughput guidance (Evora’s current profile): with 16x A100-equivalent GPUs configured for continuous batching, we target ~3.2k tokens/sec sustained with p95 < 180ms for short chat sequences (<=256 tokens). For 1k+ token requests p95 ~ 400–600ms depending on model.
- SLA language: we can offer availability and latency guardrails for the committed pool. For throughput guarantees tied to sustained tokens/sec, we’ll add an operational clause: the customer must provide representative load during the 14-day acceptance window and agree to traffic shaping if bursty jobs affect shared scheduler efficiency.
- Failure mode: if we miss acceptance thresholds we will provide a 30-day remediation plan or offer a credit for the month the miss occurred (capped at 10% of that month’s committed fees).

I’ll draft a short appendix (.md) with the numbers and a sample acceptance test harness that Evora can run from their side.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer

From: Mark Gibson <mgibson@evora-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Morris <elaine.m@evora-analytics.com>, Evora Analytics Procurement <procurement@evora-analytics.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal questions — moving from 8 to 16 GPUs

Thanks Karthik — that all looks reasonable. A couple of procurement asks:

1) Evora can commit to the 16 GPU monthly rate, but procurement requests billing for the additional 8 GPUs to begin only after their Phase 2 go-live is confirmed (we'll notify you via the acceptance test pass).
2) We need the amendment to reflect a 12-month committed term with an option to renew.
3) Please include the remediation/credit language you referenced — procurement needs it in writing.

We prefer DocuSign for the amendment. I’ve added our procurement contact CC’d here. Please send the amendment and the DocuSign link when ready.

—Mark

Attachment: evora_procurement_requirements.pdf (PDF, 28KB)

Mark / Olga / team — following up with commercial confirmation.

Commercial updates:
- Monthly committed fee (post-amendment) for 16 GPU reserved pool: see attached spreadsheet for line-item pricing and the monthly commit total.
- Transitional credit: Redwood will apply a one-time operational credit equal to 15% of the first month of Phase 2 billing if Phase 2 go-live occurs within 30 days of renewal.
- Remediation credit: as discussed, if throughput acceptance fails we’ll offer the monthly credit (capped at 10% for the impacted month) and a 30-day remediation engagement.

I attached redwood_8to16_committed_pricing.xlsx with the proposed numbers and a sample billing schedule that supports the staged start for Phase 2. If procurement is fine with DocuSign, I’ll publish the amendment and include the mutual_action_plan.md as an exhibit.

—Ben
